title: Emergencies and Reporting: What Every Missouri CDS Caregiver Should Know
description: Every CDS caregiver in Missouri is a mandated reporter. Here's what that means, the number to call (Missouri DHSS Central Registry Unit, 800-392-0210), what counts as abuse, neglect and exploitation, what to do in a medical emergency, and what to tell us.
end: Thank you for the care you give.

parts.head: Emergencies and reporting: what every CDS caregiver should know
parts.sub: What Missouri requires, and how to handle it
parts.text: Every CDS caregiver needs to know what to do in an emergency, and when to report a concern. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions CDS. Here's what Missouri requires, and how to handle it.

parts.head: You're a mandated reporter
parts.sub: Abuse, neglect or exploitation: report right away
parts.text: First, every CDS caregiver is a mandated reporter. State law requires you to report any suspicion of abuse, neglect, or exploitation, right away.

parts.sub: Missouri DHSS Central Registry Unit. Save it today.
parts.text: The number is the Missouri Department of Health and Senior Services Central Registry Unit: eight hundred, three nine two, zero two one zero. Save it in your phone today.

parts.head: Don't wait for proof
parts.sub: Unsure? Call anyway, and let them decide.
parts.text: Report immediately, not after you've gathered proof. You don't have to see it yourself. If someone tells you something that worries you, that counts too. And if you're not sure it's serious enough, call anyway, and let them decide.

parts.head: Abuse
parts.text: So what are you reporting? Abuse is any physical, sexual, or emotional harm, like hitting, rough restraint, or cruel words meant to hurt.

parts.head: Neglect
parts.sub: Not providing the care a person needs
parts.text: Neglect is failing to provide the care, food, or help a person needs and can't get on their own. It can come from carelessness, or it can be on purpose.

parts.head: Exploitation
parts.sub: Taking money or property by tricks, pressure or force
parts.text: And exploitation is taking someone's money or property by tricking, pressuring, or forcing them, like misusing a power of attorney, theft, or pressure over a will.

parts.head: Reporting isn't disloyal
parts.text: Reporting isn't disloyalty, and it isn't optional. It's how vulnerable people stay safe.

parts.head: 911 first
parts.sub: Then their emergency contact. Then us.
parts.text: In a medical emergency, call nine one one first. Then call the person's emergency contact. Then call us.

parts.head: Falls, injuries and changes
parts.sub: And any hospital or facility stay
parts.text: Tell us, and the person you care for, about any fall, injury, or sudden change in their condition. And tell us if they go into the hospital or a facility. Remember, no time can be recorded for those days.

parts.head: If the home isn't safe for you
parts.sub: Tell us. We'll work it through with you.
parts.text: Your safety matters, too. Tell us if the home ever becomes unsafe for you, or if you're threatened or mistreated. We'll work it through with you.
When you're unsure about anything, call us at 417-218-2888. Thank you for the care you give. It matters more than you know. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions CDS.
